t.name: Coleman Weedpatch Trail #121
t.description: Trail #121 starts on Forest Road 2160 a few miles before Walupt Lake Campground at the Coleman Weedpatch Trailhead. The trail heads south along the border of Goat Rocks Wilderness through dense second growth conifers and ends on the Pacific Crest Trail.

t.name: Jordan Creek Trail #94
t.description: This trail provides access to Goat Ridge above Jordan Basin within Goat Rocks Wilderness.

t.name: Goat Ridge Lookout Trail #95A
t.description: The trail climbs Goat Ridge to the former site of a fire lookout, then descends north to connect with Trail #95 again. This 1.1 mile loop offers excellent views.

t.name: Goat Ridge Trail #95
t.description: The trail climbs steeply up Goat Ridge to a junction with the Lily Basin Trail.

t.name: Snowgrass Trail #96
t.description: The trail is a major entry point to the Goat Rocks Wilderness following the Goat Creek drainage and climbing up to a junction with the Pacific Crest Trail.

t.name: Klickitat Trail #7
t.description: The 17.1 mile Klickitat Trail is a major ridgetop trail, extending from Kilborn Creek to Elk Peak. Features include ridgetop views, Castle Butte, Jackpot Lake, St. Michaels Lake, and St. John Lake.

t.name: Green Mountain Viewpoint Trail #110A
t.description: This is a short trail that climbs to the summit of Green Mountain.

t.name: Green Mountain Trail #110
t.description: This trail offers views of Mount St. Helens, Mt. Adams, and Mt. Rainier. Wild flower viewing and huckleberry picking occur along the trail as well.

t.name: Spring Creek Trail #115
t.description: Spring Creek Trail is believed to have been a Native American travel route between berry picking camps at Horseshoe Lake and fishing sites along the Cispus River. Several peeled cedar trees can be seen near the trailhead.

t.name: Killen Connector Trail #113A
t.description: Connects Horseshore Lake Campground to Killen Creek Trailhead.

t.name: Killen Creek Trail #113
t.description: Historically used for berry-picking and for sheepherding on Mt. Adams, the Killen Creek Trail climbs through forested areas and open meadows within Mt. Adams Wilderness. It offers spectacular views of Mt. Adams and meadows full of wildflowers in season.

t.name: Loop Trail #120A
t.description: Connects Keenes Trail to Horseshoe Lake.

t.name: High Lakes Trail #116
t.description: Wildflowers, huckleberries, volcanic features, high elevation lakes, and spectacular views dominate this historic trail, which was once used by Yakama Indians picking berries in the high lakes area.

t.name: Keenes Trail #120
t.description: The trail begins in the Keenes Horse Camp and provides access to Spring Creek Trail #115, High Lakes Trail #116, and Horseshoe Lake. Horses and mules share the heavily used route with hikers and bicycles as they pass through forests and meadows.

t.name: Muddy Meadows Trail #13
t.description: The Muddy Meadows trail leads into the Mount Adams Wilderness. Running through forested areas and crossing meadows it connects with the Pacific Crest Trail and ends at the High Line Trail.

t.name: Highline Trail #114
t.description: The Highline trail traveverses the north side of Mt. Adams within Mt. Adams Wilderness and rises in elevation to nearly 7,800'. The trail features spectacular views of Lyman and Lava Glaciers, as well as panoramic views of the Goat Rocks and Mt. Rainier.

t.name: Hamilton Ridge Trail #109A
t.description: This trail connects the Hamilton Buttes Trail #118 to the Hamilton Peak Tral #109.

t.name: Hamilton Peak Trail #109
t.description: The Hamilton Butte Lookout was built in 1929. The lookout was abandoned in the 1960s. Look for sections of phone line left along this trail. This historic phone line linked the lookout with the world below.

t.name: Hamilton Buttes Trail #118
t.description: On the south end, the Hamilton Buttes Trail climbs through scattered old growth and second growth forests before entering open fields on top where you get views of Mt. Adams and the Cispus River. The trail follows the ridge through several open meadows.

t.name: Blue Lake Butte Trail #119
t.description: This trail climbs steadily from Forest Road 78 for 1 mile to a semi-open ridgetop where Mt. Adams and Hamilton Buttes can be seen. The trail continues to the junction with the more heavily used Blue Lake Ridge Trail #271 near Blue Lake.

t.name: Mouse Lake Trail #271C
t.description: This short trail connects the Blue Ridge Trail #271 to Road 7812-642 passing by Mouse Lake.

t.name: Blue Lake Ridge Trail #271
t.description: This 11.7 mile multiple use trail climbs steadily through conifer forests and has heavy use. A short section of the trail above Blue Lake is "Hiker Only" to minimize noise near the lake.

t.name: Valley Trail #270
t.description: This trail has a gentle grade, with views of the Cispus River Valley and Tongue Mountain.
